<!-- nothing-1: body_md -->
\label {jbhgfdxfewae33w6q920we}
If ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $B$ is an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain, then:
$$
\text{$	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} B$ has a basic cylinder} \iff \text{$B$ is non-rigid.}
$$
<!-- end nothing-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label {edh83yf6r79hvujhxu6wrefji9e} 
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $B = \bigoplus_{i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}B_i$
an $\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$-graded affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain such that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm trdeg}}(B:B_0) \ge 2$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}} B$ has a basic cylinder $\iff$ $\exists\ d \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}} \setminus \{0\}$ such that $B^{(d)}$ is non-rigid.

\item If $B$ is normal and saturated in codimension $1$ then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerata}

\item $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}} B$ has a basic cylinder;
\item $B$ is non-rigid;
\item $B^{(d)}$ is non-rigid for some $d \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$; 
\item $B^{(d)}$ is non-rigid for all $d \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$.

\end{enumerata}
\end{enumerata}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- nothing--1: body_md -->
Let $Y$ be a normal variety with function field $K$.
We write $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}(Y)$ (resp.\ $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}_\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(Y)$) for the free $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$-module (resp.\ free $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-module) on the set of prime divisors of $Y$.
The elements of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}(Y)$ (resp.\ $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}_\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(Y)$) are called {\it divisors\/} (resp.\ {\it $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisors\/}) of $Y$. 
Two $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisors $D,D' \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}_\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}(Y)$ are {\it linearly equivalent\/} ($D \sim D'$) if $D-D' = 	\operatorname{{\rm div}}_Y(f)$ for some $f \in K^*$;
we say that  $D,D'$ are {\it $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-linearly equivalent\/} ($D \mathrel{\sim_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}}} D'$) if $nD \sim nD'$ for some integer $n>0$.
If $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}(Y)$ then the sheaf $\mathscr{O}_Y(D)$ on $Y$ is defined by
$$
\Gamma(U,\mathscr{O}_Y(D)) = \{0\} \cup \big\{\, f \in K^* \, \mid \, 	\operatorname{{\rm div}}_U(f) + D|_U \ge 0 \, \big\} \qquad \text{($\varnothing \neq U \subseteq Y$ open)}.
$$
A divisor $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}(Y)$ is {\it very ample\/} if $\mathscr{O}_Y(D)$ is a very ample invertible sheaf.
An {\it ample $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisor\/} of $Y$ is a $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisor $\Delta$ of $Y$ for which there exists an integer $n>0$ such that $n\Delta \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}(Y)$ is very ample.
Suppose that $\Delta$ is an ample $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisor of $Y$;
an open subset $U$ of $Y$ is said to be {\it $\Delta$-polar\/} if $U = Y \setminus 	\operatorname{\text{\rm supp}}(D)$ for some effective $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisor $D$ such that $D \mathrel{\sim_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}}} \Delta$.
<!-- end nothing--1 -->
<!-- nothing--2: body_md -->
Observe that if $B$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$-graded domain satisfying $e(B)=1$ then there exists a homogeneous element $t$ of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}(B)$ of degree $1$
(meaning that $t = f/g$ for some nonzero homogeneous elements $f,g \in B$ such that $\deg(f) - \deg(g) = 1$).
This is relevant in Thm \ref{jh782uwsdvvhjkqw547182}.
<!-- end nothing--2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label {jh782uwsdvvhjkqw547182}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field.
Let $B$ be an $\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$-graded normal affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain such that $e(B)=1$ and such that the number $	\operatorname{\text{\rm ht}}(B_+) = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm trdeg}}(B:B_0)$ is at least $2$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item For each homogeneous element $t$ of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}(B)$ of degree $1$,
there exists a unique $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisor $\Delta$ on the normal variety $Y = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}} B$ such that $B = \bigoplus_{m\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}} H^0(Y,\mathscr{O}_Y(m\Delta))t^m$ is an equality of rings.
Moreover, $\Delta$ has the following properties:
\begin{enumerata}

\item $\Delta$ is an ample $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisor of $Y$.

\item A nonempty open subset of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}}(B)$ is $\Delta$-polar if and only if it is basic.\footnote{An open subset $U$ of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}} B$ is {\it basic\/}
if $U = \ensuremath{\mathbb{D}}_+(f) := \big\{\, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}} B \, \mid \, f \notin {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \, \big\}$ for some homogeneous $f \in B$ of nonzero degree.}

\item $\Delta$ is Cartier if and only if $e( B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} ) = e( B )$ for all ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}} B$.

\item $\Delta \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Div}}(Y)$ if and only if $B$ is saturated in codimension $1$.

\end{enumerata}

\item If $t,t'$ are homogeneous elements of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}(B)$ of degree $1$ then the corresponding ample $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-divisors $\Delta,\Delta'$, 
defined as in part {\rm(a)}, are linearly equivalent.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label {7654cvhgfsd2d34fds23f42dfdghjk8l-geometric}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Proj}}(B)$ where
$B$ is an $\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$-graded normal affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain such that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm ht}}( B_+ ) \ge 2$.
Let $F$ be a homogeneous prime element of $B$ of degree $d>0$ and let $X = \ensuremath{\mathbb{V}}_+(F) \subset \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}$.
If the affine variety $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} \setminus X$ has a non-trivial $G_a$-action then $(B/FB)^{(d)}$ is non-rigid.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- nothing--3: body_md -->
We use ``$\setminus$'' for set difference, ``$\subset$'' for strict inclusion and  ``$\subseteq$'' for general inclusion.
We follow the convention that $0 \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$.

If $S$ is a nonempty subset of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ then $	\operatorname{\text{\rm lcm}}(S)$ is defined to be the nonnegative generator of
the ideal $\bigcap_{a \in S} a\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$.  In particular, if $S$ is an infinite subset of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ then $	\operatorname{\text{\rm lcm}}(S)=0$.
Also, $\gcd(S)$ is the nonnegative generator of the ideal of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ generated by $S$.

All rings and algebras are assumed to be associative, commutative and unital.
If $A$ is a ring then $A^*$ denotes the set of units of $A$.
If $B$ is an algebra over a ring $A$, the notation $B = A^{[n]}$ (where $n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$) means that $B$ is isomorphic as an $A$-algebra to a polynomial
ring in $n$ variables over $A$. If $L/K$ is a field extension then $L = K^{(n)}$ means that $L$ is a purely transcendental extension of $K$
of transcendence degree $n$.

The word ``domain'' means ``integral domain''.
We write $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}} A$ for the field of fractions of a domain $A$.
If ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ is a field, then a {\it ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain\/} is a domain that is also a ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-algebra;
an {\it affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain\/} (or {\it ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-affine domain}) is a domain that is a finitely generated ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-algebra.
If $A \subseteq B$ are domains then the transcendence degree of $B$ over $A$ is denoted $	\operatorname{\text{\rm trdeg}}_A(B)$ or $	\operatorname{\text{\rm trdeg}}(B:A)$.

If $A$ is a ring, we write $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(A) = \big\{\, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} A \, \mid \, 	\operatorname{\text{\rm ht}}{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}=1 \, \big\}$.

If $S$ is a subset of a group $G$, then $\langle S \rangle$ denotes the subgroup of $G$ generated by $S$.
<!-- end nothing--3 -->
<!-- nothing--4: body_md -->
\label {8736egd9fv092b5}
Let $G$ be an abelian group (with additive notation).
A {\it $G$-grading\/} of a ring $B$ is a family $\big( B_i \big)_{i \in G}$ of subgroups of $(B,+)$ satisfying $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$
and $B_iB_j\subseteq B_{i+j}$ for all $i,j \in G$.
The phrase ``let  $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a $G$-graded ring'' means that we are considering the ring $B$ together with 
the $G$-grading $\big( B_i \big)_{i \in G}$.

Let  $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a $G$-graded ring.
\begin{enumerate}

\item An element of $B$ is {\it homogeneous\/} if it belongs to $\bigcup_{i \in G} B_i$.
If $x$ is a nonzero homogeneous element, the {\it degree\/} of $x$, $\deg(x)$, is the unique $i \in G$ such that $x \in B_i$.
The degree of a non-homogeneous element is not defined.

\item $B_0$ is a subring of $B$ and is called the {\it degree-$0$ subring\/} of $B$.
If $B = B_0$, we say that the grading is {\it trivial.}

\item Given a homogeneous element $f$ of $B$, $B_{(f)}$ denotes the degree-$0$ subring of the $G$-graded ring $B_f = S^{-1}B$ where $S= \{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$.
Given a homogeneous prime ideal ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ of $B$, $B_{({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})}$ denotes the degree-$0$ subring of the $G$-graded ring
$S^{-1}B$ where $S$ is the set of homogeneous elements of $B \setminus {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$.

\item If $H$ is a subgroup of $G$, define $B^{(H)} = \bigoplus_{i \in H} B_i$ and note that 
 the inclusion $B^{(H)} \hookrightarrow B$ is a degree-preserving homomorphism of graded rings.

\item If $G=\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $B_i =0$ for all $i<0$, we say that $B$ is $\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$-graded. In this case we write $B = \bigoplus_{ i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}} } B_i$
and define $B_+ = \bigoplus_{i>0} B_i$, which is an ideal of $B$.

\item The subgroup of $G$ generated by $\big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, B_i \neq 0 \, \big\}$ is denoted $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end nothing--4 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label {983765432wevvajwklw92980}
Let $G$ be a finitely generated abelian group and $A$ a $G$-graded ring.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerata}

\item $A$ is a noetherian ring;

\item the ring $A_0$ is noetherian and the $A_0$-algebra $A$ is finitely generated;

\item every homogeneous ideal of $A$ is finitely generated.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label {98767gh11dmdffkll0ahcchvr0vfesh8263543794663cnir}
Let $A$ be a ring graded by an abelian group $G$, and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$.
\begin{enumerata}
\item If $I$ is an ideal of $A^{(H)}$ then $A^{(H)} \cap IA = I$.
\item If $A$ is noetherian then so is $A^{(H)}$.
\end{enumerata}
Moreover, if $A$ is a domain then the following hold.
\begin{enumerata}
\addtocounter{enumi}{2}

\item $A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} ) = A^{(H)}$ 

\item If $A$ is normal then so is $A^{(H)}$.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Write $A = \bigoplus_{i \in G} A_i$.
We first prove the case $H = 0$ of (a). Note that $A^{(H)} = A_0$.
Let $I$ be an ideal of $A_0$ and let $x \in A_0 \cap IA$.
Then $x = u_1 a_1 + \cdots + u_n a_n$ for some $u_1,\dots,u_n \in I$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n \in A$.
Moreover, we can arrange that $a_i$ is homogeneous and $u_i a_i \in A_0 \setminus \{0\}$ for all $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$.
We have $a_i \in A_{d_i}$ for some $d_i \in G$, and $A_0 \setminus \{0\} \ni u_i a_i \in A_{0+d_i}$, so $d_i = 0$ and hence $a_i \in A_0$ for all $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$.
Thus, $x \in I$, showing that (a) is true when $H=0$.
For the general case of (a), let $\pi : G \to \bar G = G/H$ be the canonical epimorphism and let $B = \bigoplus_{j \in \bar G}B_j$ be the
ring $A$ equipped with the $\bar G$-grading defined by $B_j = \bigoplus_{\pi(i)=j} A_i$ for each $j \in \bar G$.
Since $B_0 = A^{(H)}$ and $B=A$, the claim follows by applying the case ``$H=0$'' to $B$.
This proves (a).

(b) If $I_0 \subseteq I_1 \subseteq I_2 \subseteq \cdots$ is an infinite increasing sequence of ideals in $A^{(H)}$
then the sequence $I_0 A \subseteq I_1 A \subseteq I_2 A \subseteq \cdots$ stabilizes since $A$ is noetherian.
By (a), we have $I_n = A^{(H)} \cap I_n A$ for all $n$, so $(I_n)_{n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ stabilizes, showing that $A^{(H)}$ is noetherian.


(c) Given $x = \sum_{i \in G} x_i \in A$ (where $x_i \in A_i$ for all $i \in G$), define $S(x) =\big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, x_i \neq 0 \, \big\}$. 
We claim that
\begin{equation}  \label {2Qqs1mlkwm1oq90uvxzaAa11w4}
\text{if $x \in A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} )$ and $x \neq 0$ then $S(x) \cap H \neq \varnothing$.}
\end{equation}
Indeed, write $x = u/v$ where $u,v \in A^{(H)} \setminus \{0\}$.
Then $u\neq0$ implies $S(u) \neq \varnothing$ and $xv = u$ implies $S(u) \subseteq \big\{\, i+j \, \mid \, i \in S(x),\ j \in S(v) \, \big\}$,
so there exist $i \in S(x)$ and $j \in S(v)$ such that $i+j \in S(u) \subseteq H$;
since $j \in H$, it follows that $i \in H$, so  $S(x) \cap H \neq \varnothing$.
This proves \eqref{2Qqs1mlkwm1oq90uvxzaAa11w4}.

Now consider $x \in A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} )$. We can write $x = x_H + x'$ with $x_H,x' \in A$, $S(x_H) \subseteq H$ and $S(x') \cap H = \varnothing$.
Since $x$ and $x_H$ belong to $A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} )$, we have $x' = x - x_H \in A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} )$.
Since $S(x') \cap H = \varnothing$, \eqref{2Qqs1mlkwm1oq90uvxzaAa11w4} implies that $x'=0$, so $x = x_H \in A^{(H)}$.
Thus, $A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} ) = A^{(H)}$.

(d) If $A$ is normal then $A^{(H)} = A \cap 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}}( A^{(H)} )$ is an intersection of two normal domains and hence is normal.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label {ze3xqrctwvyjmkiu0u9inj7b2q3q01iqu}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$, let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$,
and let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $B^{(H)} \setminus \{0\}$ such that each element of $S$ is homogeneous. Then
$$
S^{-1} \big( B^{(H)} \big) = \big( S^{-1} B \big)^{(H)} \, .
$$
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Note that $S^{-1} B$ is a $G$-graded domain.
Consider $\frac{b}{s} \in S^{-1} B$ where $b$ is a homogeneous element of $B \setminus \{0\}$ and $s \in S$.
Since $\deg\big(\frac{b}{s}\big) = \deg(b) - \deg(s)$ and $\deg(s) \in H$,
we have $\deg(b) \in H$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\deg\big(\frac{b}{s}\big) \in H$, i.e.,
$\frac{b}{s} \in  S^{-1}\big( B^{(H)} \big)$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $\frac{b}{s} \in \big( S^{-1} B \big)^{(H)}$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label {0Edlv2y6ctwbeofyvrbqleuo245612nxr7m54}
Let $B$ be a ring graded by a torsion-free abelian group $G$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item  If ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} B$ and $I$ is the ideal of $B$ generated by all homogeneous elements of ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$, then $I \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} B$.

\item If $B$ is a domain, ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$ and ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ contains a nonzero homogeneous element of $B$, then ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ is a homogeneous ideal.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
(a) Since $G$ is torsion-free, there exists an order relation $\le$ on $G$ such that $(G,\le)$ is a totally ordered abelian group
(cf.\ \cite[Prop.\ 1.1.7]{AndersonFeil}); we choose such an order relation.
Proceeding by contradiction, suppose that $x,y \in B \setminus I$ are such that $xy \in I$.
Write $x = \sum_{i \in G} x_i$ and $y = \sum_{i \in G} y_i$ with $x_i,y_i \in B_i$ for all $i$.
The sets $S_x =\big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, x_i \notin I\, \big\}$ and $S_y =\big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, y_i \notin I\, \big\}$ are nonempty and finite,
so we may define $m_x = \max S_x$ and $m_y = \max S_y$. Let $x' = \sum_{i \le m_x} x_i$ and $y' = \sum_{i \le m_y} y_i$;
then $x \equiv x'$ and $y \equiv y' \pmod{I}$, so $x'y' \in I$. Moreover, if we write $x'y' = \sum_{i \in G} z_i$ with $z_i \in B_i$ for all $i$,
then $x_{m_x} y_{m_y} = z_{ m_x + m_y } \in I$,
so $x_{m_x} y_{m_y} \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$,
so $x_{m_x} \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ or $y_{m_y} \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$,
so $x_{m_x} \in I$ or $y_{m_y} \in I$, a contradiction.
This proves (a).

To prove (b), consider $I$ as in part (a) and observe that, since $	\operatorname{\text{\rm ht}}{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}=1$, ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} = I$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- bigremark-1: body_md -->
\label {iuytytsxc3welqmo9cVbvbAfvVGhue83983teij}
Of course, the above Lemma remains valid if we replace the assumption that $G$ is torsion-free
by the assumption that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion-free.
See \ref{8736egd9fv092b5} for the definition of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
<!-- end bigremark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label {i8765redfvbnki8765rfghytrew123456789iuhv}
Let $R = \bigoplus_{i \in G} R_i$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$,
let $S$ be the set of all nonzero homogeneous elements of $R$
and consider the $G$-graded domain $\EuScript{R} = S^{-1}R = \bigoplus_{ i \in G } \EuScript{R}_i$.
If $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R) \cong \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^r$ where $r \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$,
then $\EuScript{R} = \EuScript{R}_0[t_1^{\pm1}, \dots, t_r^{\pm1} ]$ where $\EuScript{R}_0$ is a field that contains $R_0$ and $t_1,\dots,t_r$ are 
nonzero homogeneous elements of $\EuScript{R}$ that are algebraically independent over $\EuScript{R}_0$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
We may assume that $r \neq 0$.
Observe that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(\EuScript{R}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R) \cong \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^r$.
Since every nonzero homogeneous element of $\EuScript{R}$ is a unit, we have $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(\EuScript{R}) = \big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, \EuScript{R}_i \neq 0 \, \big\}$,
so we can choose nonzero homogeneous elements $t_1,\dots,t_r$ of $\EuScript{R}$ such that $( \deg(t_j) )_{j=1}^r$ is a basis of the free $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$-module $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(\EuScript{R})$. 
The reader can check that $\EuScript{R}_0$ and $t_1,\dots,t_r$ have the desired properties.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label {8hVCixdCN95g2ZRB3iAcxzqe}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field and $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ a ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-algebra graded by an abelian group $G$.
If ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} \subseteq B_0$, we say that the grading is {\it over\/} ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$, or that $B$ is graded {\it over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$\/} by $G$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- bigremark-2: body_md -->
\label {ijn3eoocnnqppieudbc}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field, $B$ a ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain and $G$ an abelian group.
If ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$ or $G$ is torsion-free then every $G$-grading of $B$ is over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$.
However, this is not true for arbitrary ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ and $G$.
For example, the $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$-algebra $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$ admits a $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}/2\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$-grading that is not over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$
(namely, $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} \oplus \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} i$).
<!-- end bigremark-2 -->
<!-- bigremark-3: body_md -->
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field and $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G}B_i$ an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
If the grading is over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ then $B$ is finitely generated as a $B_0$-algebra and $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is a finitely generated group.
Here is an example showing that these conclusions are not necessarily valid when the grading is not over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$.

Let $R = \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}[ (\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}},+) ]$ be the group ring of the group $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}},+)$.
The elements of $R$ are
formal sums $\sum_{q \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}} a_q t^q$ where $a_q \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$ for all $q$ and $a_q \neq 0$ for at most finitely many $q$,
and where the family $(t^q)_{q \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}}$ satisfies $t^q t^r = t^{q+r}$ for all $q,r \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$.
Consider the subfield ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}( (t^q)_{q \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}} )$ of the field of fractions of $R$;
note that $t$ is transcendental over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$ and that ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} / \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}(t)$ is an algebraic extension of infinite degree.
For each $q \in I = [0,1) \cap \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$, consider the subspace $V_q = \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}(t)t^q$ of the vector space ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}(t)$.
Then ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} = \bigoplus_{q \in I} V_q$.
Let $G = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}/\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ and let $\pi : \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}} \to G$ be the canonical homomorphism of the quotient.
Then $\pi|_I : I \to G$ is bijective; let $\varphi : G \to I$ be the inverse of $\pi|_I$.
So we have ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} = \bigoplus_{g \in G} V_{\varphi(g)} = \bigoplus_{g \in G} {\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}_g$ where we define ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}_g = V_{\varphi(g)}$ for all $g \in G$.
This is a $G$-grading of ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ such that ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}_0 = \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}(t)$.
So ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ is a $G$-graded affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain, ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ is not finitely generated as a ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}_0$-algebra, and $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}({\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}) = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}/\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ is not finitely generated.
<!-- end bigremark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label {kcjviyc2e2w45w6d2o9kmgvczxwer}
Let $G$ be an abelian group, $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ a $G$-graded ring, and $R$ a subring of $B_0$.
If $B$ is finitely generated as an $R$-algebra then so is $B^{(H)}$ for every subgroup $H$ of $G$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label {8Qp98781hy2uexihvcx2qw2wUxq3ew0pokjmnbvaw2345}
If ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ is a field and $B$ is an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain graded over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ by an abelian group $G$,
then $B^{(H)}$ is an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain for every subgroup $H$ of $G$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since the grading is over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$, this follows from Lemma \ref{kcjviyc2e2w45w6d2o9kmgvczxwer}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
Given a domain $B$ graded by an abelian group $G$,
we write $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ for the set of subgroups $H$ of $G$ such that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)/(H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B))$ is torsion.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- bigremark-4: body_md -->
\label {kDjkbwevCdcojBh6qvmAxfea7u}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
\begin{enumerate}

\item Let $\mathscr{T}(G)$ be the set of subgroups $H$ of $G$ such that $G/H$ is torsion.
Then $\mathscr{T}(G) \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, and equality holds if and only if $G/\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion.
Thus, if $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)=G$ then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B) = \mathscr{T}(G)$.

\item $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion if and only if $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ is the set of all subgroups of $G$.
In particular, if $G$ is a finite group then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ is the set of all subgroups of $G$.

\item If $G = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ and the grading is nontrivial then  $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ is the set of all nonzero subgroups of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$.

\item If $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ then $B$ is an integral extension of $B^{(H)}$.
Indeed, if $b \in B \setminus \{0\}$ is homogeneous then $\deg(b) \in \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, so there exists $n\ge1$ such that $n \deg(b) \in H$
and hence $b^n \in B^{(H)}$.

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end bigremark-4 -->
<!-- bigremark-5: body_md -->
When dealing with a single $G$-graded ring $B$, it is often convenient to assume that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)=G$,
as this typically simplifies definitions, results, and even proofs. 
In the present work, however, we must formulate many definitions and results (for instance the definition of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$)
without this simplifying assumption, because we frequently consider several graded rings simultaneously---for example,
inclusions $B^{(H)} \subseteq B^{(K)} \subseteq B$ where $H \subseteq K$ are subgroups of $G$.
<!-- end bigremark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label {87654esxcvs9dfok33me4rtu5ortyo0934urud3r24}
Let $B$ be a noetherian normal domain graded by an abelian group $G$, and let $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item $	\operatorname{\text{\rm ht}}(J) = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm ht}}(J \cap B^{(H)})$ for every ideal $J$ of $B$.

\item The map $f : 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} B \to 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} B^{(H)}$, $f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) = {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \cap B^{(H)}$,
is surjective and satisfies $f^{-1} \big( 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1 B^{(H)} \big) = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1 B$.

\item If $G$ is torsion-free then $f^{-1}(Z') = Z$,
where $Z$ (resp.\ $Z'$) denotes the set of height $1$ homogeneous prime ideals of $B$ (resp.\ $B^{(H)}$).
Moreover, $f|_Z : Z \to Z'$ is bijective.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{98767gh11dmdffkll0ahcchvr0vfesh8263543794663cnir}, $B^{(H)}$ is a noetherian normal domain;
moreover, $B$ is integral over $B^{(H)}$ by Rem.\ \ref{kDjkbwevCdcojBh6qvmAxfea7u}(4).
By \cite[(5.E)]{Matsumura}, the Going-Down Theorem holds for $B^{(H)} \subseteq B$;
so assertion (a) follows from \cite[(13.C)]{Matsumura}, and (b) follows from (a).
Now assume that $G$ is torsion-free. If ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1 B$ and ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1 B^{(H)}$ are such that $f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) = {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$,
then Lemma \ref{0Edlv2y6ctwbeofyvrbqleuo245612nxr7m54}(b) implies that ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}$ is homogeneous if and only if ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ is homogeneous.
So $f^{-1}(Z') = Z$ by part (b), which also implies that $f|_Z : Z \to Z'$ is surjective.
Consider ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in Z'$ and ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_1, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_2 \in Z$ such that $f( {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_1 ) = {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} = f( {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_2 )$.
If $x$ is a nonzero homogeneous element of ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_1$ then we may choose $d\ge1$ such that $x^d \in B^{(H)}$;
then $x^d \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \subseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_2$ and hence $x \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_2$, showing that ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_1 \subseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_2$. By symmetry, ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_1 = {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}_2$.
So $f|_Z$ is bijective and (c) is proved.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label {jBh9823hedAcv78n2erj20}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.

If $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ and $M$ is a submonoid of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ then $\langle H \cap M \rangle = H \cap \langle M \rangle$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
It is clear that  $\langle H \cap M \rangle \subseteq H \cap \langle M \rangle$.
For the reverse inclusion, consider $i \in H \cap \langle M \rangle$.
Since $i \in \langle M \rangle$ and $M$ is a monoid, there exist $j_1,j_2 \in M$ such that $i = j_1 - j_2$.
Since $j_1 \in \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ and $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, there exists $n>0$ such that $(n+1) j_1 \in H$.
Define $i_1 = (n+1)j_1$ and $i_2 = j_2 + nj_1$. Then $i_1 \in H \cap M$, $i_2 \in M$, and
$$
H \ni i = (j_1 + nj_1) - (j_2 + nj_1) = i_1 - i_2,
$$
so $i_2 \in H$, i.e., $i_2 \in H \cap M$. So $i =  i_1 - i_2 \in \langle H \cap M \rangle$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label {GOfBH}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
$$
\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) \quad \text{for all $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.}
$$
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Consider the submonoid $M = \big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, B_i \neq 0 \, \big\}$ of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$. Then $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \langle M \rangle$ and
$\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) = \langle H \cap M \rangle = H \cap \langle M \rangle = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ by Lemma \ref{jBh9823hedAcv78n2erj20}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label {765tgc2wvtegrlkjmn098b27qw6qesrxcvac23rjpa}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$. 
For every subgroup $H$ of $G$,
$$
\text{$H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ $\iff$ $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) / \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} )$ is torsion.}
$$
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
It is clear that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) \subseteq H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, so there is a surjective group homomorphism
$\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) / \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) \to \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)/(H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B))$ and consequently $(\Leftarrow)$ is true.
Conversely, if $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ then  $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) / \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)/(H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B))$ by Lemma \ref{GOfBH},
and since  $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)/(H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B))$ is torsion it follows that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)/\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} )$ is torsion, so $(\Rightarrow)$ is true.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label {6543wxcvbnc3wvlplpo0i9kijh7waq4rtmlb87hg}
Let $S$ be a multiplicative set of a domain $R$ of characteristic $0$ and let $D : S^{-1}R \to S^{-1}R$ be a derivation.
Suppose that $R$ is finitely generated as an algebra over the ring $R \cap \ker(D)$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item There exists $s \in S$ such that the derivation $sD : S^{-1}R \to S^{-1}R$ maps $R$ into itself.
Consequently, $(sD)|_R : R \to R$ is a derivation of $R$.

\item If $D$ is locally nilpotent then so are $sD$ and $(sD)|_R$.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label {SliceThm}
Let $B$ be a $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-algebra, $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm LND}}(B)$ and $A = \ker(D)$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item If $s\in B$ satisfies $Ds=1$ then $B = A[s] = A^{[1]}$ and $D = \frac{d}{ds} : A[s] \to A[s]$.

\item Let $t \in B$ be such that $D(t) \neq 0$ and $D^2(t)=0$, and let $a = D(t) \in A\setminus\{0\}$.
Then $B_a = A_a[t] = (A_a)^{[1]}$.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label {ldkjxhcvi82ewdj0wd}
Let $A \subseteq B$ be domains of characteristic $0$ such that $B$ is integral over $A$.
If $\delta : A \to A$ is a locally nilpotent derivation and $D : B \to B$ is a derivation that extends $\delta$,
then $D$ is locally nilpotent.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label {8hnvnBbslijvxbgxsab8AbN7p03msS726rfXC}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a ring graded by an abelian group $G$.
\begin{enumerate}

\item A derivation $D : B \to B$ is {\it homogeneous\/} if there exists $d \in G$ such that $D(B_i) \subseteq B_{i+d}$ holds for all $i \in G$;
if $D$ is homogeneous and nonzero then $d$ is unique, and is called the {\it degree\/} of $D$.

\item $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) = \big\{\, D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm LND}}(B) \, \mid \, \text{$D$ is homogeneous} \, \big\}$

\item $	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B) = \big\{\, \ker(D) \, \mid \, D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) \text{ and } D \neq 0 \, \big\}$

\item We say that $B$ is {\it rigid\/} if $	\operatorname{\text{\rm LND}}(B) = \{0\}$, and {\it graded-rigid\/} if $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) = \{0\}$.

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label {876543wsdfgxhnm290cAo}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $B$ an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain graded by a torsion-free abelian group $G$.
Then,
$$
	\operatorname{\text{\rm LND}}(B) = \{0\} \ \iff \ 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) = \{0\} .
$$
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label {876543wqzxcvbnmC9l03ord}
Let $\EuScript{B}$ be a domain of characteristic $0$ graded by an abelian group $G$ and suppose that $\EuScript{B} = R[t] = R^{[1]}$
where $R$ is a graded subring of $\EuScript{B}$ and $t$ is homogeneous.
For each $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B})$, we have $R^{(H)} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}\big(\EuScript{B}^{(H)}\big)$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Let $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B})$ and note that $I=\big\{\, m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \, \mid \, m \deg(t) \in H+\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R) \, \big\}$ is a nonzero ideal of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$.
Let $n>0$ be such that $I = n\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$.  We claim that 
\begin{equation} \label {i765re5dsdv78394itjgh}
\text{there exists $i \in G$ such that $R_i \neq 0$ and $i+ n\deg(t) \in H$.}
\end{equation}
Indeed, we have $n \deg(t) \in \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R) + H$, so we may choose $g \in \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R)$ and $h \in H$ such that $n\deg(t) = g+h$.
Since $M=\big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, R_i \neq 0 \, \big\}$ is closed under addition and the subgroup of $G$ generated by $M$ is $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R)$,
we have $g = i_1 - i_2$ for some $i_1, i_2 \in M$. Since $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B})$, there exists $m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$ such that $m i_1 \in H$.
Define $i = (m-1)i_1 + i_2$, then $i \in M$ (so $R_i\neq0$) and $i+n\deg(t) = (m-1)i_1 + i_2 + g + h = mi_1+h \in H$,
which proves \eqref{i765re5dsdv78394itjgh}.

Choose $i$ as in \eqref{i765re5dsdv78394itjgh}, choose $\rho \in R_i \setminus \{0\}$,
and choose $d \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$ such that $d i \in H$ ($d$ exists because $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B})$).
Define $\xi = \rho^d$ and $\tau = \rho t^n$; these are nonzero homogeneous elements of $R^{(H)}$ and $\EuScript{B}^{(H)}$ respectively,
and $\tau$ is transcendental over $R^{(H)}$.
We claim that 
\begin{equation}  \label {78ytu765ededyv3pmr0i9}
R^{(H)}[\tau] \subseteq \EuScript{B}^{(H)} \subseteq \big(R^{(H)}\big)_\xi [\tau] .
\end{equation}
The first part of \eqref{78ytu765ededyv3pmr0i9} is clear.
To prove the second part, note that
each element of $\EuScript{B}^{(H)}$ is a finite sum of elements of the form $rt^m$ where $r$ is a homogeneous element of $R\setminus\{0\}$, $m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$,
and $\deg(rt^m) \in H$. For such an element $rt^m$, we have $\deg(r) + m\deg(t) \in H$ and $\deg(r) \in \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(R)$,
so $m \in I = n\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ and hence $m = nk$ for some $k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$.
Then $rt^m = r (t^n)^k = r \rho^{-k} \tau^k$.
Choose $\ell \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ such that $\ell d -k \ge0$; then 
\begin{equation}  \label {p8utr4w3q2mc0nbtd}
\textstyle
r t^m = \frac{r \rho^{ \ell d-k }}{\xi^\ell} \tau^k \, .
\end{equation}
Since $\deg(rt^m), \deg(\xi), \deg(\tau) \in H$, \eqref{p8utr4w3q2mc0nbtd} gives $\deg( r \rho^{ \ell d-k } ) \in H$,
so $r \rho^{ \ell d-k } \in R^{(H)}$ and hence $rt^m \in \big(R^{(H)}\big)_\xi [\tau]$ by \eqref{p8utr4w3q2mc0nbtd} again.
This proves $\EuScript{B}^{(H)} \subseteq \big(R^{(H)}\big)_\xi [\tau]$ and completes the proof of \eqref{78ytu765ededyv3pmr0i9}.

Now  \eqref{78ytu765ededyv3pmr0i9} implies that $\big(\EuScript{B}^{(H)}\big)_\xi = S[\tau] = S^{[1]}$ where $S= \big(R^{(H)}\big)_\xi$,
so we may consider the derivative $\frac{d}{d\tau} : S[\tau] \to S[\tau]$.
Let $\Delta = \xi \frac{d}{d\tau} : (\EuScript{B}^{(H)} )_\xi \to (\EuScript{B}^{(H)} )_\xi$;
then $\Delta \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}} \big( (\EuScript{B}^{(H)} )_\xi  \big)$ and $\ker \Delta = S$.
We claim that $\Delta(\EuScript{B}^{(H)}) \subseteq \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$.
To see this, consider the same element $rt^m$ as before and let us check that $\Delta(rt^m) \in \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$.
If $m=0$ then $\deg(r) = \deg(rt^m) \in H$, so $rt^m = r \in R^{(H)}$ and hence $\Delta(rt^m) = 0 \in \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$.
If $m>0$ then $k>0$, so \eqref{p8utr4w3q2mc0nbtd} gives
$$
\textstyle
(\EuScript{B}^{(H)} )_\xi \ni \Delta(rt^m)
=  \xi \frac{d}{d\tau}\big( \frac{r \rho^{ \ell d-k }}{\xi^\ell} \tau^k \big)
= \xi \cdot \frac{r \rho^{ \ell d-k }}{\xi^\ell} \cdot  k \tau^{k-1} = k r \rho^{d-1} t^{n(k-1)} \in \EuScript{B} .
$$
Since $\EuScript{B} \cap (\EuScript{B}^{(H)} )_\xi = \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$ by Lemma \ref{98767gh11dmdffkll0ahcchvr0vfesh8263543794663cnir}, we get $\Delta(rt^m) \in \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$.
Since every element of $\EuScript{B}^{(H)}$ is a finite sum of elements  $rt^m$ of this type, we obtain $\Delta(\EuScript{B}^{(H)}) \subseteq \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$.
Let $D : \EuScript{B}^{(H)} \to \EuScript{B}^{(H)}$ be the restriction of $\Delta$.
Then $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}\big( \EuScript{B}^{(H)} \big)$ and $\ker D = \EuScript{B}^{(H)} \cap \ker\Delta = \EuScript{B}^{(H)} \cap \big(R^{(H)}\big)_\xi$.
Since $R$ is factorially closed
in $\EuScript{B} = R^{[1]}$, it follows that $R^{(H)}$ is factorially closed in $\EuScript{B}^{(H)}$,
so $\EuScript{B}^{(H)} \cap \big(R^{(H)}\big)_\xi = R^{(H)}$ and hence $\ker D = R^{(H)}$.
We have $D(\tau) = \xi \frac{d}{d\tau}(\tau) = \xi \neq 0$, so $D \neq 0$ and hence $R^{(H)} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}\big(\EuScript{B}^{(H)}\big)$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label {8237e9d1983hdjyev93}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $B$ be an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain graded over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ by an abelian group $G$, and let $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item For each $A \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B)$, we have $A^{(H)} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B^{(H)})$.

\item The map $	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B) \to 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B^{(H)})$, $A \mapsto A^{(H)}$, is injective.

\item If $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) \neq \{0\}$ then $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B^{(H)}) \neq \{0\}$.

\item If $G$ is torsion-free and $B$ is non-rigid then $B^{(H)}$ is non-rigid.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
(a) Let $A \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B)$.
Choose $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) \setminus \{0\}$ such that $\ker D = A$, and choose a homogeneous element $t \in B$ such that $D(t)\neq 0$ and $D^2(t)=0$.
Consider the homogeneous element $a = D(t)$ of $A\setminus\{0\}$ and
let $\EuScript{B} = B_a$ and $R=A_a$; then $\EuScript{B} = R[t] = R^{[1]}$ by Lemma \ref{SliceThm}(b).
Since $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(\EuScript{B}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, we have $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B}) = \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ and hence $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B})$;
so  $R^{(H)} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}\big(\EuScript{B}^{(H)}\big)$ by Lemma \ref{876543wqzxcvbnmC9l03ord}.
Choose $\Delta \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( \EuScript{B}^{(H)} )$ such that $\ker(\Delta) = R^{(H)}$.

Since $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, there exists $n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$ such that $\deg(a^n) \in H$; let $\alpha = a^n$ and observe that $\EuScript{B} = B_\alpha$.
By Lemma \ref{ze3xqrctwvyjmkiu0u9inj7b2q3q01iqu},  we have $\EuScript{B}^{(H)} = \big( B_\alpha \big)^{(H)} = \big( B^{(H)} \big)_\alpha$, so
$\Delta \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}\big( ( B^{(H)} )_\alpha \big)$.
Since (by Cor.\ \ref{8Qp98781hy2uexihvcx2qw2wUxq3ew0pokjmnbvaw2345}) $B^{(H)}$ is ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-affine,
Lemma \ref{6543wxcvbnc3wvlplpo0i9kijh7waq4rtmlb87hg} implies that there exists $\ell \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$
such that $\alpha^\ell\Delta : ( B^{(H)} )_\alpha \to ( B^{(H)} )_\alpha$ maps $B^{(H)}$ into itself.
Let $\delta : B^{(H)} \to B^{(H)}$ be the restriction of $\alpha^\ell\Delta$; then $\delta \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( B^{(H)} )$
and $\ker(\delta) = B^{(H)} \cap \ker(\Delta)  = B^{(H)} \cap R^{(H)}$. To finish the proof of (a), it suffices to
verify that 
\begin{equation}  \label {f4ergc3t9ruw9eidmfcngh}
B^{(H)} \cap R^{(H)} = A^{(H)} \quad \text{and} \quad A^{(H)} \neq B^{(H)} .
\end{equation}
The fact that $A$ is factorially closed in $B$ implies that $B \cap R = B \cap A_a = A$, so 
$$
A^{(H)} \subseteq B^{(H)} \cap R^{(H)}  \subseteq B^{(H)} \cap B \cap R = B^{(H)} \cap A = A^{(H)} ,
$$
which proves the first part of \eqref{f4ergc3t9ruw9eidmfcngh}.
To prove the second part, recall that $D(t) \neq 0$.
Since $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, we can pick $m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$ such that $t^m \in B^{(H)}$.
Since  $D(t^m) = mt^{m-1}D(t)\neq0$, we have $t^m \notin A$, so $t^m \notin A^{(H)}$ and hence $A^{(H)} \neq B^{(H)}$.
So \eqref{f4ergc3t9ruw9eidmfcngh} is true and assertion (a) is proved.

(b) Suppose that $A_1,A_2 \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm KHLND}}(B)$ are such that $A_1^{(H)} =A_2^{(H)}$.
Consider a nonzero homogeneous element $a \in A_1$. Since $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, we can pick $m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}\setminus\{0\}$ such that $a^m \in A_1^{(H)}$.
Then $a^m \in A_2^{(H)} \subseteq A_2$, so $a \in A_2$ since $A_2$ is factorially closed in $B$.
This shows that $A_1 \subseteq A_2$, and $A_1=A_2$ follows by symmetry. This proves (b).

Part (c) is an obvious consequence of part (a).

(d) Since $G$ is torsion-free and $B$ is ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-affine and non-rigid,
Lemma \ref{876543wsdfgxhnm290cAo} implies that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) \neq \{0\}$, so $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B^{(H)}) \neq \{0\}$ by (c), so $B^{(H)}$ is non-rigid.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- bigremark-6: body_md -->
It is easy to produce examples showing that the converses to (c) and (d) are false.
If (a) is reformulated as an ``if-then'' statement, its converse is also false.
Moreover, the Theorem itself is false if we do not assume that $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.
For instance, consider the polynomial ring $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}[X,Y]$ with the $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$-grading defined by declaring that $X$ and $Y$ are 
homogeneous of degrees $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, respectively. Let $B$ be the $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$-graded subalgebra $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}[X^2,X^3,Y]$ of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}[X,Y]$.
Then $0 \neq \frac{\partial}{\partial Y} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B)$ but if $H$ is the subgroup of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ generated by $(1,0)$
then $B^{(H)} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}[X^2,X^3]$ is rigid. So all assertions of the Theorem are false for this choice of $H$.
<!-- end bigremark-6 -->
<!-- bigremark-7: body_md -->
\label {8765r984f5f7637w}
If $B$ is a ring of characteristic $0$ (graded or not), the 
{\it Makar-Limanov invariant\/} of $B$ (denoted $	\operatorname{\text{\rm ML}}(B)$)
is the intersection of the kernels of all elements of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm LND}}(B)$.
If $B$ is graded, define the {\it homogeneous Makar-Limanov invariant\/} of $B$ (denoted $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HML}}(B)$)
to be the intersection of the kernels of all elements of $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B)$.
Note that if $B$ is graded then $	\operatorname{\text{\rm ML}}(B) \subseteq 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HML}}(B)$.

Thm \ref{8237e9d1983hdjyev93} implies that
if ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ is a field of characteristic $0$ and $B$ an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain graded over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ by an abelian group $G$,
then $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HML}}(B^{(H)}) \subseteq 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HML}}(B)^{(H)}$ for every $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.
<!-- end bigremark-7 -->
<!-- notation-2: body_md -->
\label {7823689wuehdb4xei8ibc}
If $B$ is a domain of characteristic $0$ graded by an abelian group, let 
$$
\mathscr{X}(B) = \big\{\, H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B) \, \mid \, 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( B^{(H)} ) \neq \{0\} \, \big\} .
$$
<!-- end notation-2 -->
<!-- bigremark-8: body_md -->
\label {6543wscvhyuhoblgmrne4b3vf432wsdfw}
Let $B$ be a domain of characteristic $0$ graded by an abelian group.
\begin{enumerata}

\item $\mathscr{X}(B) \subseteq \big\{\, H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B) \, \mid \, \text{$B^{(H)}$ is non-rigid} \, \big\}$

\item If $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion-free and $B$ is a finitely generated algebra over a field,
then equality holds in part (a), by Lemma \ref{876543wsdfgxhnm290cAo}.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end bigremark-8 -->
<!-- notation-3: body_md -->
\label {Zlknckjhi7evoenvnbCgEybgdCgbfpr9t839of}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.  For each $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, we define 
$$
\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B) = \big\{\, H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B) \, \mid \, H' \subseteq H \, \big\} .
$$
<!-- end notation-3 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label {3Pkj762cx7bXckayscxcvi8Y025esxcZxbkq}
Given a domain $B$ graded by an abelian group $G$,
\begin{equation*}
\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}( B^{(H)} ) = \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B) \quad \text{for all $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.
Since $B^{(H)}$ is an $H$-graded ring, $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}( B^{(H)} )$ is a collection of subgroups of $H$;
clearly,  $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B)$ too is a collection of subgroups of $H$.
So it suffices to show that, for each subgroup $H'$ of $H$, we have $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}( B^{(H)} ) \Leftrightarrow H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.
Let $H'$ be a subgroup of $H$.
Let $U = H' \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B)$, $V = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ and $W = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, and note that $U \subseteq V \subseteq W$ and (since $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$) $W/V$ is torsion;
so $V/U$ is torsion if and only if $W/U$ is torsion.
Since $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)}) = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ by Lemma \ref{GOfBH}, we have
$\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) / ( H' \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) ) = (H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)) / ( H' \cap H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B) ) = V/U$,
so $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}( B^{(H)} )$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $V/U$ is torsion.  Hence,
$H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}( B^{(H)} ) \Leftrightarrow \text{$V / U$ is torsion} \Leftrightarrow \text{$W / U$ is torsion} \Leftrightarrow H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$,
as desired.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label {8A273gLbv9ncxcavcbo3w982376re5}
Let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $B$ an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain graded over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ by an abelian group $G$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item If $H \in \mathscr{X}(B)$ then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B) \subseteq \mathscr{X}(B)$.


\item Let $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ and let $T$ be the torsion subgroup of $H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
If $B^{(H)}$ is non-rigid then so is $B^{(H')}$ for every $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ such that $T \subseteq H' \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) \subseteq H$.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
(a) Let $H \in \mathscr{X}(B)$.  By Cor.\ \ref{8Qp98781hy2uexihvcx2qw2wUxq3ew0pokjmnbvaw2345}, $\EuScript{B} = B^{(H)}$ is an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain; clearly,
$\EuScript{B}$ is graded by $H$ and this grading is over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$.
Since $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(\EuScript{B}) \neq \{0\}$ (because $H \in \mathscr{X}(B)$), 
Thm \ref{8237e9d1983hdjyev93} implies that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( \EuScript{B}^{(H')} ) \neq \{0\}$ for all $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B})$;
we have $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\EuScript{B}) = \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B)$ by Lemma \ref{3Pkj762cx7bXckayscxcvi8Y025esxcZxbkq},
and for each $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B)$ we have $H' \subseteq H$ and hence $\EuScript{B}^{(H')} = B^{(H')}$,
so $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( B^{(H')} ) \neq \{0\}$ (and hence $H' \in \mathscr{X}(B)$) for all $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_H(B)$. 

(b) As in part (a), the ring $\EuScript{B} = B^{(H)}$ is an affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain and is graded over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ by $H$.
We have $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \EuScript{B} ) = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ by Lemma \ref{GOfBH}, so the torsion subgroup of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \EuScript{B} )$ is $T$ and the group $\Omega = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \EuScript{B} ) / T$ is torsion-free.
Let $\pi : \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(\EuScript{B}) \to \Omega$ be the canonical homomorphism of the quotient and let
$\bar\EuScript{B}$ denote the ring $\EuScript{B}$ equipped with the $\Omega$-grading $\bar\EuScript{B} = \bigoplus_{\omega \in \Omega} \bar\EuScript{B}_\omega$
where (for each $\omega \in \Omega$) $\bar\EuScript{B}_\omega = \bigoplus_{ \pi(i)=\omega } \EuScript{B}_i$.
Since $\bar\EuScript{B}$ is a non-rigid affine ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$-domain and $\Omega$ is torsion-free,
Lemma \ref{876543wsdfgxhnm290cAo} gives $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( \bar\EuScript{B} ) \neq \{0\}$ and hence $\Omega \in \mathscr{X}(\bar\EuScript{B})$.
Since the grading of $\bar\EuScript{B}$ is over ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$, (a) implies that  $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}_\Omega(\bar\EuScript{B}) \subseteq \mathscr{X}(\bar\EuScript{B})$,
i.e., $\ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\bar\EuScript{B}) \subseteq \mathscr{X}(\bar\EuScript{B})$.
In particular, $\bar\EuScript{B}^{(W)}$ is non-rigid for each $W \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\bar\EuScript{B})$;
we have the equalities of non-graded rings $\bar\EuScript{B}^{(W)} = \EuScript{B}^{(\pi^{-1}(W))} = (B^{(H)})^{(\pi^{-1}(W))} = B^{(\pi^{-1}(W))}$, so 
\begin{equation}  \label {98ujedws65tgawieryhqstrdfuuiwis09oiubvcccftbmhyxdb65}
\text{$B^{(\pi^{-1}(W))}$ is non-rigid for every  $W \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\bar\EuScript{B})$.}
\end{equation}
Consider $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ such that $T \subseteq H' \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) \subseteq H$; we show that $B^{(H')}$ is non-rigid.
We have $B^{(H')} = B^{(H'')}$ where we set $H'' = H' \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
Since $\ker\pi \subseteq H'' \subseteq 	\operatorname{\text{\rm dom}}\pi$, if we define $W = \pi(H'')$ then $H'' = \pi^{-1}(W)$.
We claim that $\Omega / W$ is torsion.
To see this, consider $\omega \in \Omega$.
Choose $i \in \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \EuScript{B} ) = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ such that $\pi(i)=\omega$.
Since $H' \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$, there exists $n\ge1$ such that $ni \in H' \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = H''$; then $n\omega = \pi(ni) \in \pi(H'') = W$,
which shows that $\Omega / W$ is torsion and hence $W \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(\bar\EuScript{B})$.
By \eqref{98ujedws65tgawieryhqstrdfuuiwis09oiubvcccftbmhyxdb65},
$B^{(H')} = B^{(H'')} = B^{(\pi^{-1}(W))}$ is non-rigid.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label {oi8y81726et73e8f0i349rtfyh-sat}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
Given ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}} B$,
the set $\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, B_i \nsubseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \, \big\}$ is a submonoid of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
The subgroup of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ generated by $\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ is denoted $\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$.
We define the subgroup $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ of $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ by
$$
\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \begin{cases}
\bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) }\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) & \text{if $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \neq \varnothing$,} \\
\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) & \text{if $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) = \varnothing$.}
\end{cases}
$$
We say that $B$ is {\it saturated in codimension $1$\/} if $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label {o72ytg8ed623orh9yft8v1238293y}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
If ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ is a homogeneous prime ideal of $B$ then $\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Clearly, $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by
$\big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, (B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})_i \neq 0 \, \big\} = \big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, B_i \nsubseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \, \big\} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$,
so $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label {3498huv8oe98y3876wgebf09}
Let $B$ be a domain of characteristic $0$ graded by an abelian group~$G$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item For each $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) \setminus \{0\}$,
there exists a height $1$ homogeneous prime ideal ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ of $B$ satisfying:
\begin{enumerata}
\item some homogeneous element $t \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ satisfies $D(t) \neq 0$ and $D^2(t)=0$;
\item $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D )$.
\end{enumerata}

\item $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) \subseteq \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D ) \subseteq \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ for all $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B)$.

\item If $B$ is saturated in codimension $1$ then $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ for all $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B)$.


\end{enumerata}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
(a) Let $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B) \setminus \{0\}$ and let $A = \ker D$.
Choose a homogeneous $t \in B$ such that $Dt \in A\setminus\{0\}$. 
Let $S$ be the set of homogeneous elements of $A \setminus \{0\}$.
Note that $S^{-1}B$ and $S^{-1}A$ are $G$-graded $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-domains, $S^{-1}D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}( S^{-1}B ) \setminus \{0\}$ and $\ker(S^{-1}D) = S^{-1}A$.
Since $(S^{-1}D)(t)$ is a unit of $S^{-1}A$, we have $S^{-1}B = (S^{-1}A)[t] = (S^{-1}A)^{[1]}$ by Lemma \ref{SliceThm}.
The condition $S^{-1}B = (S^{-1}A)[t] = (S^{-1}A)^{[1]}$ implies that
${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} = t S^{-1}B$ is a height $1$ prime ideal of $S^{-1}B$.
By basic properties of localization, it follows that ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} = B \cap {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}$ is a height $1$ prime ideal of $B$.
It is clear that ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}$ is homogeneous, so ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ is homogeneous.
We have $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( S^{-1}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( S^{-1}B/tS^{-1}B ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(S^{-1}A) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(A)$ and $t \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$, so (a) is proved.

(b) Let $D \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B)$. It is clear that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D ) \subseteq \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, so it's enough to prove
that $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) \subseteq \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D )$.  If $D = 0$ then the claim is obvious.
If $D\neq0$ then part (a) implies that there exists a height $1$ homogeneous prime ideal ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ of $B$
such that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$.
We have $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} )$ by Lemma \ref{o72ytg8ed623orh9yft8v1238293y}, so $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D ) = \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} )$.
Since ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$ we have $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \neq \varnothing$, so 
$\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) =\bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{q}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) } \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{q}}} ) \subseteq\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} ) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( \ker D )$,
which proves (b).

(c) The assumption means that $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, so this follows from (b).
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label {eibuw9x6hAvpjwua6w3rh61s298746}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
If $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion and $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \neq \varnothing$ then 
$$
\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) } \!\! {\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})
\ = \ \big\{\, i \in G \, \mid \, \text{$B_i \nsubseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ for every ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$} \, \big\} .
$$
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Since every submonoid of a torsion group is a group, we have $\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$
for each ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$. The conclusion follows.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label {o98hfng54ye9c72ye6fv11vbdi38}
Let $B$ be a domain graded by an abelian group $G$.
Assume that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion-free and let $Z$ denote the set of all height $1$ homogeneous prime ideals of $B$.
If $Z \neq \varnothing$ then $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in Z } \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} )$,
and if $Z = \varnothing$ then $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let the notation be $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$.
Observe that the claim is true if $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) = \varnothing$, and assume that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \neq \varnothing$.
Then $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)} \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$, so it suffices to show that
\begin{equation} \label {2wsedqrwge0oihkvmnbtfrewqaswdfgxvbcnxmz}
\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \begin{cases}
\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) & \text{if ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in Z$,} \\
\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) & \text{if ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in  	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \setminus Z$.}
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
If ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in Z$ then $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ by Lemma \ref{o72ytg8ed623orh9yft8v1238293y}.
If ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \setminus Z$ then Lemma \ref{0Edlv2y6ctwbeofyvrbqleuo245612nxr7m54}(b)
(together with Rem.\ \ref{iuytytsxc3welqmo9cVbvbAfvVGhue83983teij} and the fact that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is torsion-free)
implies that $B_i \cap {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} = \{0\}$ for all $i \in G$,
so $B_i \nsubseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ for all $i \in G$ such that $B_i\neq0$, so $\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label {89fDCN584uKHJu7u59034uf}
Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a $G$-graded domain that is finitely generated as a $B_0$-algebra.
\begin{enumerata}

\item Let $S$ be a finite generating set of the $B_0$-algebra $B$ such that each element of $S$ is nonzero and homogeneous.
Let ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B)$ and define  $D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} = \big\{\, \deg(x) \, \mid \, x \in S \setminus {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \, \big\}$.
Then ${\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ is the submonoid of $G$ generated by $D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$,
and $\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by $D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$.

\item The set $\big\{\, \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} ) \, \mid \, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B) \, \big\}$ is finite.

\item The set $\big\{\, \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B/{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}) \, \mid \, \text{${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B)$ and ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$ is homogeneous} \, \big\}$ is finite.

\item Let $S$ be as in part {\rm(a)} and let $P$ be the set of all ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$ satisfying ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \cap S \neq \varnothing$.  Then
$$
\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \begin{cases}
\bigcap_{{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in P} \langle D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \rangle  & \text{if $P \neq \varnothing$,} \\
\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)  & \text{if $P = \varnothing$.}
\end{cases}
$$

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
It is straightforward to see that if ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B)$ then ${\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ is the submonoid of $G$ generated by $D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$
(we leave this to the reader).
This implies that $\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by $D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}}$, so (a) follows.
Since $D = \big\{\, \deg(x) \, \mid \, x \in S \, \big\}$ is a finite set,
and since $\big\{\, D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \, \mid \, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B) \, \big\}$ is a collection of subsets of $D$,
we see that $\big\{\, D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \, \mid \, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B) \, \big\}$ is a finite set; so (b) follows from (a).
In view of Lemma \ref{o72ytg8ed623orh9yft8v1238293y}, (c) follows from (b).
To prove (d), we first note that the claim is true if $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)=\varnothing$; so we may assume that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \neq \varnothing$,
which implies that
$\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)} \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})
= \bigcap_{{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)} \langle D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \rangle$ by (a).
Moreover, we have $\langle D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \rangle = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ for each ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in  	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) \setminus P$, so the desired conclusion follows.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- bigremark-9: body_md -->
\label {iutr3nic34ri34765io21p}
If $B$ is a noetherian domain graded by a finitely generated abelian group,
then Thm \ref{983765432wevvajwklw92980} implies that $B$ is finitely generated as a $B_0$-algebra,
so the hypothesis of Proposition \ref{89fDCN584uKHJu7u59034uf} is satisfied.
<!-- end bigremark-9 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
It is usually fairly easy to compute $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
As an example, let ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}$ be a field and $R = {\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}[ U, V, X, Y ] = {\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}^{[4]}$ the polynomial ring graded by $G = \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}/42\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$,
where ${\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}} \subseteq R_{\bar0}$ and $U, V, X, Y$ are homogeneous of degrees $\overline{15}, \overline{14}, \overline{18}, \overline{24}$ respectively,
where $\overline{m}$ is the image of $m \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ by the canonical epimorphism $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \to G$.
Then $f = U^4 V^6 + X^3 Y^2 \in R_{\overline{18}}$, so $B = R/fR = {\ensuremath{\rm \bf k}}[u,v,x,y]$ is a $G$-graded domain.
We use Prop.\ \ref{89fDCN584uKHJu7u59034uf}(d) with $S = \{u,v,x,y\}$. Then $P = \{ (u,x) , (u,y) , (v,x) , (v,y) \}$.
If ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} = (u,x)$ then $\langle D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \rangle = \langle \overline{14}, \overline{24} \rangle = \langle \bar{2} \rangle$. 
In this way, we find $\big\{\, \langle D_{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \rangle \, \mid \, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in P \, \big\} = \{ \langle \bar{2} \rangle, \langle \bar{3} \rangle \}$
and hence $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \langle \bar{2} \rangle \cap \langle \bar{3} \rangle  = \langle \bar{6} \rangle$.
Note that $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = G$, so $B$ is not saturated in codimension $1$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label {GandGbarOfBH}
If $B$ is a noetherian normal domain graded by an abelian group,
$$
\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}( B^{(H)} ) = H \cap \operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) \quad \text{for all $H \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$.}
$$
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Consider the map $f : 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B) \to 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}(B^{(H)})$, ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \mapsto {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \cap B^{(H)}$,
and the sets $Z = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$  and $Z' = 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B^{(H)})$.
By Lemma \ref{87654esxcvs9dfok33me4rtu5ortyo0934urud3r24}(b), $f$ is surjective and $f^{-1}(Z') = Z$. Thus,
\begin{equation}  \label {P892hXDrkynmXyZaMgnubvbn0MiNh587645r6uiw}
\text{$f|_Z : Z \to Z'$ is well-defined and surjective.}
\end{equation}
In particular, $Z = \varnothing$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $Z' = \varnothing$.
If $Z = \varnothing = Z'$ then $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ and $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)})$, so Lemma \ref{GOfBH} gives
$\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)}) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)}) = H \cap \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = H \cap \operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$, as desired.
If $Z = \varnothing = Z'$ is false then $Z \neq \varnothing$ and $Z' \neq \varnothing$, so
$\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \in Z } \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} )$
and $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)}) = \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in Z' } \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B^{(H)}, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} )$.
We claim:
\begin{equation}  \label {8xm1evgfc1e2910rcpawijgqzw}
H \cap \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} ) = \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B^{(H)}, f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) ) \quad \text{for all ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \in Z$.}
\end{equation}
Indeed, if ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \in Z$ then
$$
\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}( B^{(H)}, f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) )
= \big\{\, i \in H \, \mid \, B_i \nsubseteq f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) \, \big\}
= \big\{\, i \in H \, \mid \, B_i \nsubseteq {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \, \big\}
= H \cap \ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) ,
$$
so $\overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B^{(H)}, f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) )
= \langle H \cap \ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) \rangle
= H \cap \langle \ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) \rangle
= H \cap \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} )$ by Lemma \ref{jBh9823hedAcv78n2erj20},
which proves \eqref{8xm1evgfc1e2910rcpawijgqzw}.
Statements \eqref{8xm1evgfc1e2910rcpawijgqzw} and \eqref{P892hXDrkynmXyZaMgnubvbn0MiNh587645r6uiw} give the second and third equalities in:
\begin{align*}
H \cap \operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) &= \textstyle  \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \in Z } \big( H \cap \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} ) \big)
=  \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}} \in Z } \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B^{(H)}, f({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{P}}}) ) \\
&= \textstyle \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in Z' } \overline{\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}( B^{(H)}, {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} )
= \operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B^{(H)}) .
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- notation-4: body_md -->
\label {98w3gvddb9wudjcudj}
We write $(A,B) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$ as an abbreviation for:
\begin{quote}
\it $A$ is a ring, $B$ is an $A$-algebra, and for every derivation $\delta : A \to A$ there exists a unique derivation $D: B \to B$
that makes the following diagram commute:
$$
\xymatrix@R=12pt{
B \ar[r]^D & B \\
A \ar[u] \ar[r]^{\delta} & A \, . \ar[u]
}
$$
\end{quote}
<!-- end notation-4 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
\label {83uedxc5trfnbvcDFVUirybhnjYMYbgfAcfiu736}
If $L/K$ is a separable algebraic field extension, then $(K,L) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$ (see \cite{Zar-Sam_CommAlg1}, Corollary $2'$, p.~125).
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label {piud29hdbfdu74heqoir923ft7fbc1oeyt}
Let $B$ be a domain of characteristic $0$ graded by an abelian group $G$.
Suppose that $H_1,H_2 \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{T}}(B)$ satisfy $H_1 \subseteq H_2$ and $(B^{(H_1)},B^{(H_2)}) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$.
\begin{enumerata}

\item Suppose that $\delta : B^{(H_1)} \to B^{(H_1)}$ is a derivation and that $D: B^{(H_2)} \to B^{(H_2)}$ is the unique derivation of $B^{(H_2)}$ that extends it.
If $\delta$ is locally nilpotent (resp.\ homogeneous) then so is $D$.

\item If $B^{(H_1)}$ is non-rigid then so is $B^{(H_2)}$.

\item If $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B^{(H_1)}) \neq \{0\}$ then $	\operatorname{\text{\rm HLND}}(B^{(H_2)}) \neq \{0\}$.

\end{enumerata}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
(a) If $\delta$ is locally nilpotent then, since $B^{(H_2)}$ is integral over $B^{(H_1)}$,
$D$ is locally nilpotent by Lemma \ref{ldkjxhcvi82ewdj0wd}.
Suppose that $\delta$ is homogeneous; let $d \in H_1$ be such that $\delta(B_j) \subseteq B_{j+d}$ for all $j \in H_1$.
Consider $b \in B_i \setminus\{0\}$ where $i \in H_2$.
Choose $n\ge1$ such that $ni \in H_1$.
We have $b^n \in B_{ni} \subseteq B^{(H_1)}$, so $nb^{n-1}D(b)= D(b^n) =\delta(b^n) \in B_{ni+d}$.
Since $nb^{n-1} \in B_{(n-1)i} \setminus \{0\}$ and $nb^{n-1}D(b) \in B_{ni+d}$,
it follows that $D(b) \in B_{i+d}$. This shows that $D(B_i) \subseteq B_{i+d}$ for all $i \in H_2$, i.e., $D$ is homogeneous.
This proves (a), and assertions (b) and (c) easily follow from (a).
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label {dh2763g5d4fc5a4dsErf56w7}
Let $B$ be a noetherian normal domain and $A$ a subring of $B$.
Suppose that $(	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}} A , 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Frac}} B ) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$ and that
there exists a family $( f_i )_{i \in I}$ of elements of $A \setminus \{0\}$ satisfying:
\begin{itemize}

\item $(A_{f_i},B_{f_i}) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$ for every $i \in I$;

\item no height $1$ prime ideal of $B$ contains all $f_i$.

\end{itemize}
Then $(A,B) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label {nvo2983epdk02qkw0}
Let $A$ be a ring, $A[\mathbf{X}] = A[X_1,\dots,X_n] = A^{[n]}$, $f_1,\dots,f_n \in A[\mathbf{X}]$, $B = A[\mathbf{X}]/(f_1,\dots,f_n)$,
and $\pi : A[\mathbf{X}] \to B$ the canonical homomorphism of the quotient ring.
Let $P \in A[\mathbf{X}]$ be the determinant of the Jacobian matrix $\frac{\partial(f_1,\dots,f_n)}{\partial(X_1,\dots,X_n)}$.
If $\pi(P)$ is a unit of $B$, then $(A,B) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label {5eghxWiC2j3mjfnjahvfcd56yui}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-domain graded by a finite abelian group $G$.
Suppose that there exist homogeneous units $x_1, \dots, x_n \in B^*$ such that
$\langle \deg x_1 \rangle \oplus \cdots \oplus \langle \deg x_n \rangle = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
Then $(B_0,B) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
We may assume that $\deg(x_i) \neq 0$ for all $i$.
For each $i=1,\dots,n$, let $e_i\ge2$ be the order of $\deg(x_i)$ in $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$.
Let $L = \big\{\, ( {\ell_1}, \dots, {\ell_n} ) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}^n \, \mid \, \text{$0 \le \ell_i < e_i$ for all $i = 1,\dots,n$} \, \big\}$
and observe that the map $( {\ell_1}, \dots, {\ell_n} ) \mapsto \deg( x_1^{\ell_1} \cdots x_n^{\ell_n} )$ from $L$ to $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B)$ is bijective.
This implies that if $b$ is a nonzero homogeneous element of $B$ then there is a unique $( {\ell_1}, \dots, {\ell_n} ) \in L$
such that $\deg(b) =  \deg( x_1^{\ell_1} \cdots x_n^{\ell_n} )$; since $x_1,\dots,x_n$ are homogeneous units of $B$, it follows
that $b /( x_1^{\ell_1} \cdots x_n^{\ell_n} ) \in B_0$, so $b = a x_1^{\ell_1} \cdots x_n^{\ell_n}$ for some $a \in B_0$.
This shows that $B$ is a free $B_0$-module with basis
$\EuScript{B} = \big\{\, x_1^{\ell_1} \cdots x_n^{\ell_n} \, \mid \, ( {\ell_1}, \dots, {\ell_n} ) \in L \, \big\}$.


Consider the ideal $I =(X_1^{e_1}-x_1^{e_1}, \dots, X_n^{e_n}-x_n^{e_n})$ of the polynomial ring $B_0[X_1,\dots,X_n]$
and the surjective homomorphism of $B_0$-algebras $\varphi : B_0[X_1,\dots,X_n] \to B$ given by $\varphi(X_i) = x_i$ ($1 \le i \le n$).
Clearly, $I \subseteq \ker\varphi$.
If $F \in \ker\varphi$ then the division algorithm shows that 
there exists $f \in B_0[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ such that $F \equiv f \pmod{I}$ and $\deg_{X_i}(f)<e_i$ for all $i=1,\dots,n$;
then $f \in \ker\varphi$, so $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=0$, so the fact that $\EuScript{B}$ is linearly independent over $B_0$ implies that $f=0$.
This shows that $\ker\varphi=I$, so 
$$
B \cong B_0[X_1,\dots,X_n] / (X_1^{e_1}-x_1^{e_1}, \dots, X_n^{e_n}-x_n^{e_n})  .
$$
Let $P \in B_0[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ be the determinant of the Jacobian matrix
$\frac{\partial(X_1^{e_1}-x_1^{e_1}, \dots, X_n^{e_n}-x_n^{e_n})}{\partial(X_1,\dots,X_n)}$.
Since $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}} \subseteq B$, $P(x_1,\dots,x_n) = \prod_{i=1}^n ( e_i x_i^{e_i-1} )$ is a unit of $B$;
so $(B_0,B) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$ by Lemma \ref{nvo2983epdk02qkw0}.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Let $B$ be a domain graded by a finite abelian group $G$.
An element $x$ of $B$ is {\it admissible\/} if there exist nonzero homogeneous elements $x_1,\dots,x_n$ of $B$
such that $x = x_1x_2\cdots x_n$ and $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \langle \deg(x_1) \rangle \oplus \cdots \oplus \langle \deg(x_n) \rangle$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label {d8iuyhv1i288wsx9}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}$-domain graded by a finite abelian group $G$.
If $x$ is an admissible element of $B$ and $m\ge1$ is such that $x^m \in B_0$,
then $( (B_0)_{x^m} ,B_{x^m} ) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
There exist nonzero homogeneous elements $x_1,\dots,x_n$ of $B$
such that $x = x_1x_2\cdots x_n$ and $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \langle \deg(x_1) \rangle \oplus \cdots \oplus \langle \deg(x_n) \rangle$.
Consider the $G$-graded domain $\EuScript{B} = B_{x^m}$ and note that $x_1, \dots, x_n$ are homogeneous units of $\EuScript{B}$ such that
$\langle \deg x_1 \rangle \oplus \cdots \oplus \langle \deg x_n \rangle = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(\EuScript{B})$.
By Lemma \ref{5eghxWiC2j3mjfnjahvfcd56yui}, we have $(\EuScript{B}_0,\EuScript{B}) \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm EXT}}$.
Since (by Lemma \ref{ze3xqrctwvyjmkiu0u9inj7b2q3q01iqu} with $H=0$) $\EuScript{B}_0 = (B_0)_{x^m}$, we are done.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label {98876152r3ediwof93408eh}
Let $B = \bigoplus_{i \in G} B_i$ be a domain graded by a finite abelian group $G$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerati}

\item $B$ is saturated in codimension $1$;
\item no height $1$ prime ideal of $B$ contains all admissible elements of $B$.

\end{enumerati}
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
If $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)=\varnothing$ then both (i) and (ii) are true, so (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii).
From now on, assume that $	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)\neq\varnothing$.
Note that $\operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) } {\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$ by Lemma \ref{eibuw9x6hAvpjwua6w3rh61s298746}.

Suppose that (i) holds.
Then $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \operatorname{\bar\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \bigcap_{ {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B) } {\ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$.
Consider ${\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}} \in 	\operatorname{\text{\rm Spec}}^1(B)$. Then $\operatorname{\ensuremath{\mathbb{G}}}(B) = \ensuremath{\mathbb{M}}(B,{\ensuremath{\mathfrak{p}}})$.
